proposal.title: Disable Blosc bitshuffle for lower-CPU LZ4 full-field reads
proposal.hypothesis: Operational evidence shows the measured consumer workload is warm-cache shuffled full-field tensor access over 28 samples, and provider/cache download changes cannot improve consumer_samples_per_second. With the current one-sample full-field chunks, each sample read pays both LZ4 decompression and Blosc bit-unshuffle work for three large float32 channel chunks. If the chunks keep the same layout and LZ4 codec but disable the bitshuffle preconditioner, the consumer should spend less CPU per decoded full-field sample and increase consumer_samples_per_second while preserving frozen array paths, coordinates, selector dimensions, validation, provenance, rerun behavior, dependencies, Zarr v3 consolidated publication, and semantic values.
proposal.expected_tradeoffs: Output bytes will likely increase because LZ4 will see unshuffled float32 byte streams, and materialization time may change modestly from writing larger chunks with less shuffle CPU. The intended isolated gain is higher warm-read throughput.

edits.rationale: Keeps the public Zarr layout and LZ4 compression path unchanged while removing the Blosc bit-unshuffle transform from every warm full-field chunk read.

proposal.validation_plan: Rerun the evaluator and confirm contract_correctness, semantic_equivalence, provenance_security, and rerun_safety still pass. Compare consumer_samples_per_second against the current 81.51 samples/s, while monitoring output_bytes and materialization_seconds as tradeoffs.
